definition: Outlier means a person or thing lying far outside the usual range or pattern.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word outlier. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know outlier should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Nine of the ten repair quotes clustered around 400 dollars; the outlier, at 65, came from a contractor who had misread the blueprints.
A rarity is merely uncommon — a left-handed catcher — and stops well short of an outlier.
An anomaly goes further than a rarity — it genuinely departs from the expected pattern — but it stops short of an outlier, which lies measurably far outside the entire range.

An exception breaks the rule — the one case a policy does not cover — though it may sit close to the pattern in every other way. An outlier need not break any rule at all: it is defined by measured distance, lying far outside the usual range. Exceptions defy rules; outliers defy averages.

An oddity is simply a strange item — it catches the eye, and no measurement is involved. An outlier passes no judgment on strangeness: it is a case lying far from a crowd of ordinary ones, and it can be the best, the worst, or merely the farthest.

Outlier is a measuring word — it means a person or thing lying far outside the usual range, and it implies a crowd of ordinary cases to lie outside of.
Unlike 'oddity,' it passes no judgment on strangeness: an outlier can be the best, the worst, or merely the farthest, but it is always alone out there.
Outlier is the number-cruncher's noun, at home wherever there is a distribution to sit outside of — scores, rainfall, salaries.
In this unit it pairs with aberrant: aberrant is the adjective for behavior that breaks the pattern, outlier the noun for the case sitting far from it.
An exception merely breaks a rule; an outlier is measured by its distance.

For the statistics unit, Mr.
Okafor's class measured thirty bean seedlings they had planted on the same day.
Twenty-nine of the plants stood between ten and fourteen centimeters tall, a tidy cluster the students graphed with satisfaction.
Plant eleven was the outlier: forty-one centimeters, towering so far above the rest that it bent the class average upward by itself.
Some students wanted to erase it and keep the neat graph; others argued that a measurement so far outside the range must have a cause.
The cause turned up on Friday — a cracked pipe had been quietly watering plant eleven's corner of the tray all month.
